name: Baseline engagement journey
description: A sequential fictional decomposition of the inherited 192-hour, nine-month baseline.
assumptions: The stages are sequential, so elapsed days are summed.
One modeled month equals 30 modeled days; this is an educational convention, not a procurement convention.
The original cookbook supplied only 192 total hours and nine months, so every stage allocation is a new modeled assumption.

stages.description: Identify and initially qualify the fictional opportunity.
assumptions: Initial qualification consumes intermittent work across two modeled weeks.

stages.description: Establish an internal sponsor for continued exploration.
assumptions: Sponsor alignment is modeled without a detailed stakeholder topology.

stages.description: Understand the workflow problem and intervention boundary.
assumptions: Workshops and synthesis are active effort within a longer calendar window.

stages.description: Validate feasibility of the bounded workflow layer.
assumptions: Validation does not implement the solution or replace authoritative systems.

stages.description: Review modeled access and governance constraints at a high level.
assumptions: This is a stage allocation, not a detailed security governance model.

stages.description: Determine a generic route to authorization and purchase.
assumptions: No real procedure or named contract vehicle is represented.

stages.description: Prepare and revise the fictional commercial proposal.
assumptions: The proposal is distinct from contract negotiation.

stages.description: Resolve the fictional agreement and its terms.
assumptions: Elapsed time includes calendar delay, not continuous legal labor.

stages.description: Obtain authorization to begin the bounded implementation.
assumptions: Approval is kept visible and is not a detailed governance workflow.

stages.description: Confirm engagement closure and readiness for implementation handoff.
assumptions: Acceptance closes this buying journey; it is not product acceptance testing.
